source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 9: Values of lambda for which A and B are singular (book page 60).

blocks.prompt: 9. Find the values of \(\lambda\) if \(A\) and \(B\) are singular. \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & \lambda & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & \lambda & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)
blocks.explanation:
Singular matrix woh square matrix hai jis ka determinant zero ho (aur is liye us ka inverse nahi hota).
To humein \(|A| = 0\) aur \(|B| = 0\) rakh kar \(\lambda\) nikalna hai.
Plan: dono determinants expand karein (\(\lambda\) sirf ek dafa aata hai, to linear equation banegi), zero ke barabar rakhein, solve karein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & \lambda & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & \lambda & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), dono singular.
Humein find karna hai: \(A\) ke liye \(\lambda\) aur \(B\) ke liye \(\lambda\) (dono alag sawal hain).
Tareeqa: Singular ka matlab \(|A| = 0\). Row 1 ke along expansion.

\(|A|\) ko row 1 ke along expand karein
\[|A| = 4(\lambda - 18) - 2(7 - 12) + 3(21 - 2\lambda)\]
\[= 4\lambda - 72 + 10 + 63 - 6\lambda\]
\[= 1 - 2\lambda\]
Kyun: Minors: \(\lambda \cdot 1 - 6 \cdot 3 = \lambda - 18\), \(7 \cdot 1 - 6 \cdot 2 = -5\), \(7 \cdot 3 - \lambda \cdot 2 = 21 - 2\lambda\). Signs \(+,\,-,\,+\): \(-2(-5) = +10\). Phir \(4\lambda - 6\lambda = -2\lambda\) aur \(-72 + 10 + 63 = 1\).

\(|A| = 0\) solve karein
\[1 - 2\lambda = 0\]
\[\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(A\) singular tabhi hoga jab determinant zero ho.

\(|B|\) ko row 1 ke along expand karein
\[|B| = -2(0 - \lambda) - 4(0 - 2) + 5(\lambda + 4)\]
\[= 2\lambda + 8 + 5\lambda + 20\]
\[= 7\lambda + 28\]
Kyun: Minors: \((-2)(0) - (1)(\lambda) = -\lambda\), \((1)(0) - (1)(2) = -2\), \((1)(\lambda) - (-2)(2) = \lambda + 4\). Entry \(-2\) aur minor \(-\lambda\) ka product \(+2\lambda\); \(-4 \times (-2) = +8\).
Dhyan dein: Entry ka sign, position ka sign aur minor ka sign teeno alag hain; har term ko bracket mein likhein.

\(|B| = 0\) solve karein
\[7\lambda + 28 = 0\]
\[\lambda = -4\]
Kyun: 28 ko doosri taraf le ja kar 7 se divide kiya.

Tasdeeq
\[\lambda = \tfrac{1}{2}:\ |A| = 1 - 1 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[|B| = 7(-4) + 28 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Values wapas rakhne se dono determinants zero aaye, yani dono matrices singular hain.
blocks.final_answer: \(A\) singular hai jab \(\lambda = \frac{1}{2}\); \(B\) singular hai jab \(\lambda = -4\).
